name: AGC 200232 (Hubble)
blurb: AGC 200232, a gas-rich dwarf galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: agc200232-hubble
story: An extremely low-mass dwarf galaxy, rich in hydrogen gas and first noticed by a radio survey. Hubble picked out its brightest red giant stars to pin down its distance.

claims.text: AGC 200232 is a SHIELD II target of Hubble program 13750, 'Fundamental Parameters of the SHIELD II Galaxies'
SHIELD galaxies are gas-rich dwarf galaxies
SHIELD galaxies were selected from the ALFALFA radio (HI) survey catalog
The Hubble imaging was used to measure distances from the tip of the red giant branch
A TRGB distance was measured for AGC 200232
SHIELD targets are extremely low-mass galaxies
